title: Rakab Ganj Is Reclaimed With Affidavits and Ceremony

blocks.text: Resistance to Sikh claims in Delhi is broken partly by force and partly by political management. Written affidavits are gathered, pressure is applied through intermediaries such as Ram Dyal, and the necessary permissions are assembled before direct action is taken.

With those papers in hand, Baghel Singh moves on the site of Rakab Ganj associated with Guru Tegh Bahadur's cremation. Demolition of the obstructing structure is ordered, the Khalsa standard is raised, and the place is publicly re-marked as Sikh sacred ground.

The page closes in liturgical rather than military fashion. Sacred kharh-parshad is distributed and ceremony seals the reclamation, showing how legal maneuver, force, and devotion are made to work together.
